lineage.strategy: Add authorization-path evidence for Aurora-INL to distinguish regulatory execution from test-reactor and manufacturing milestones.

observations.fact: DOE Idaho Operations Office approved the Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis for the Aurora powerhouse at Idaho National Laboratory under the Reactor Pilot Program, covering preliminary hazard analysis, accident analysis, safety controls and design commitments.
Oklo states Aurora-INL has access to recovered EBR-II fuel and is advancing alongside its Aurora Fuel Fabrication Facility, whose PDSA had already been approved in December 2025.

risks.risk: DOE Reactor Pilot Program authorization is not equivalent to NRC commercial licensing; Oklo states it intends to pursue NRC licensing for commercial operations, so commercial regulatory risk remains.

unknowns.unknown: The source does not establish final DOE operating authorization, NRC commercial license approval, commercial power revenue, or plant-level cost economics.

recommendation: Credit the PDSA approval as concrete regulatory-execution evidence while keeping final authorization, NRC commercialization and economic proof separate and unresolved.
